name: Style the control
description: See how a switch gets its color and motion from data-state, including the indeterminate state, and when attrs belong on your own element.

steps.title: The example styles it
steps.task: This switch has a color, and the thumb moves. Those styles are classes in the example. The component does not include them.
steps.hint: Switch renders the button and sets data-state. The classes in the example turn that state into a color and a position.
steps.learn: See that the styling is in the example

steps.title: Turned on
steps.task: We turned it on. data-state is now checked, and that is what moved the thumb. The example does not change a class from script.
steps.hint: The root, the track, and the thumb all get the same data-state. The label next to the switch is ordinary text.

steps.title: The track
steps.task: The color is on the track. Off, its class is bg-surface-variant. Checked, data-[state=checked]:bg-primary replaces it.
steps.hint: The thumb in this example stays white. Change the track classes when you want different on and off colors.

steps.title: The thumb
steps.task: The thumb stays white. It moves from translate-x-1 to translate-x-6 when data-state is checked, and it stays visible either way.
steps.hint: transition-transform on the thumb is what animates that move. Without it, the thumb jumps to the new position.

steps.title: The class that moved it
steps.task: We opened the source. The thumb classes are translate-x-1 and data-[state=checked]:translate-x-6. Changing data-state is what runs the transition.
steps.hint: The track classes are on the line above: bg-surface-variant and data-[state=checked]:bg-primary. The same pattern works for your own switch.
steps.learn: Find the data-state class in the example source

steps.title: Style the attribute
steps.task: data-state is checked, unchecked, or indeterminate. Style those values with CSS. You do not need a second class in script that copies the state.
steps.hint: If script and the component both track the state, they can disagree. data-state is already updated when the switch changes.
steps.learn: Style data-state instead of toggling a class

steps.title: Which part has it
steps.task: data-state is on the root, the track, and the thumb. data-disabled is on the root and on SelectAll, and its only value is true.
steps.hint: Check the Components column before you write a selector. The track and the thumb do not have data-disabled.
steps.learn: See which part sets which attribute

steps.title: Missing, not false
steps.task: data-disabled is either true, or it is left off the element. false would still match a data-disabled selector, so the component omits the attribute instead.
steps.hint: This block fades the root with data-[disabled]:opacity-50. The track and the thumb fade with it, because they do not have their own data-disabled.
steps.learn: See why data-disabled is true or missing

steps.title: Indeterminate
steps.task: Enable all is indeterminate. Some settings are on and some are off, so the thumb sits in the middle of the track.
steps.hint: The track is a lighter primary in this state. aria-checked is still false.

steps.title: ARIA and CSS
steps.task: aria-checked is for assistive technology. data-state is for CSS. An indeterminate switch has data-state indeterminate and aria-checked false.
steps.hint: Enable all looks half on, but a screen reader announces it as off. aria-checked has no third value.

steps.title: Bind attrs once
steps.task: This block is renderless, so attrs goes on the element you render. The default root is a button and already has attrs. Putting attrs on a child as well runs the click twice.
steps.hint: Use renderless when you want to replace the button. If you are styling that button, you do not need renderless.
steps.learn: Bind slot attrs only on a renderless host

steps.title: That's the look
steps.task: The component sets the state. You style data-state. Put attrs on your own element only when renderless replaces the button.
steps.hint: Checkbox uses the same three data-state values. Radio has checked and unchecked only.
steps.learn: Style the next headless control the same way
